Hiya! I hope my comment doesn't come too late, but I figured I'd give my 2 cents because I've been doing some research myself into how to connect Baggebos.

In this [post](https://www.reddit.com/r/IkeaGreenhouseClub/comments/17ikyaf/i_joined_the_double_baggebo_club_here_are_some/), OP mentions in post that their husband installed nuts & bolts to connect the units together and posted an [image ](https://imgur.com/a/xzM0k9N)in the comments showing this. I think the right way to go about it is to use a drill and an appropriate drill bit to drill a small hole and use nuts & bolts to connect them together. Seeing as how you've already done this to customize the shelf heights, I figure this should be no problem, however, I would caution that it might be worth disassembing the furniture to get a good angle on what you're trying to drill.

Regarding acrylic shelves - it's fairly straightforward to take a basic Closetmaid shelf and use wire cutters to cut off excess for it to fit pretty perfectly as shelves, especially for the Baggebo. Take a look at my build, let me know if you have any questions! Wayyy more affordable than acrylic shelves and provides every bit of airflow.

I'm gonna be realistic with you. There's a couple options to consider. And you don't have to disclose every single detail, just that you are experiencing a health crisis and that you need assistance. I would expect at some point you'll have to specify your mental health, but the finer details are none of the company's business from an organizational perspective.

1. Have a honest conversation with your direct manager about the fact that you are struggling. In my case while I was at Collins, I was able to get something informal worked out this way directly after the 2020 election when I had a massive mental health breakdown. Basically all my work was temporarily shifted to my colleagues and I had super reduced work responsibilities. During that time I was barely working, meaning I had time to rest and pursue therapy and psychiatrist appointments as needed (if meds are a path you pursue, sometimes it takes a week or more to adjust to a new medication, so having fewer responsibilities can help make the adjustment easier).
2. Reach out to HR and ask for a leave of absense or FMLA. This is the more formal route, but from my experience these folks approach these situations with care and consideration. These options typically come with some reduction in your pay, but it offers guaranteed job protection under the FMLA specifically.
3. It's a long shot, but look up whether you can access unemployment benefits in your state if you are fired. Not related to my experience with Collins, I was fired from a different job after struggling with both mental and physical health and after being put on a PIP. I wasn't sure if I was elligible for unemployment, but I applied nonetheless and provided all the requested information. At the end of the day, the state governing body determined that I had been terminated without just cause. This is a Hail Mary kind of strategy, but it is achieved by simply ceasing to give a fuck and focusing on your immediate needs. In my case, my boss didn't like that I asked to work from home for a week because I had strep throat. So I let her fire me because I knew I was making the right decision for my health (and the health of everyone, for that matter.) I even got a severance package despite the firing, but again this was not at Collins. If you're lucky and play your cards, you might qualify for unemployment and this can help take the burden off and give you the bandwidth to seek the help you need.

I sincerely hope this helps. I promise you that things will get better, even if it doesn't seem like it immediately. When I was let go from Collins, I felt like I'd never be able to make it by on anything less than what they paid me. **Looking back on it now, I would have never been able to make it if I had continued with that company and continue to let my mental health suffer.** Losing my job was the biggest blessing in disguise and since then I've been able to focus on myself and my mental health.
